name: Church of the Earthmother — Why It's Stone

text.content:
Why a humble nature-goddess has a grand stone cathedral — the surface answer, the real one, and the crack it hides. The player handout plants the unease; this is what it's for.

What the villagers say (and the handout plants): the church is gratitude in stone — generations of thanks for harvests that never fail, poured into finer masonry than a village this size should be able to afford. That's true as far as it goes, and it is meant to sit slightly wrong: the Earthmother is a humble god of granges and gardens, and a poor valley does not raise cathedrals to her.

The truth: that impossible plenty is the Dreamer's grief overflowing as good weather and heavy harvests. The church is gratitude architecture funded by a weeping fey and raised over her resting place — a beautiful, expensive monument to a comfortable lie, addressed to a goddess who has never once answered. A rich church to a humble god is Greenrest entire, in stone.

If a player pulls on the thread

  • Religion / History: the iconography is subtly wrong for Chauntea — a winged, blossoming figure in the tympanum, star-and-sun motifs, grove-and-fey trappings throughout — closer to the local “Green Lady” than the orthodox Earthmother. A religion-trained PC clocks it as not-quite-Chauntean: the first real crack.
  • The altar's offerings and the harvest-rites face the great tree in the square, not the granary.
  • Let the grandeur do the work — the handout already makes a thoughtful player uneasy; reward anyone who leans in, but never confirm the secret here.
